titre: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth Director David Fincher Sparks Backlash for 'Wildly Dystopian' Vision of AI-powered Filmmaking
chapo: Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.
extrait: Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Fincher, who directed Seven, Fight Club, and The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, has reunited with long-term collaborator Brad Pitt for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, which was written by Quentin Tarantino. It is a standalone sequel and spinoff to Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, with Pitt reprising his role as stunt double Cliff Booth. In a recent interview with Sean Fennessey on The Ringer’s Big Picture podcast, Fincher confirmed that he used AI to sync the best take of a line reading with the best performance take when they didn’t align on camera, in order to speed up production by cutting down the number of takes needed. Essentially, he used AI to replace dialogue and adjust actors’ lip movements in post-production. “We could use AI to re-lip that thing,” he said. “So it was freeing, it was the freeing up of… think of this entirely plastically. We’re not chiseling this out of marble. We’re working with plasticine. You know what I mean? Just giving ourselves that freedom to go, ‘what is the best thing on the eye, and then what is the best thing on the ear,’ and f***ing do not worry about how we’re going to get there, because we will figure out a way. And we did, in most cases. I think there’s a couple of shots [that] didn’t quite work, but they’re getting there. By the time it’s on service.” Fincher added that the actors spent just a handful of days re-recording dialogue. Dialogue replacement was just 5% conventionally done, the rest “all AI.” But it was his comments made later in the interview, where Fincher described how he sees directing with AI going in the future, that have sparked the most vociferous response. “I’m imagining — and what I’ve seen with AI technology — I’m imagining a world in the next year where everything that humans do great, like sculpting, painting, ageing, blowing fake spider’s webs into the corner, smoking up a volume, putting a shaft of light in it, putting a crazy f***ing wig on somebody, doing all their makeup… like, I can imagine a world where — and I don’t think we’re far away — you hire all the same people. titre: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth Director Explains His Use of AI
chapo: Commonly known for his high take count, David Fincher now uses AI to shorten production, as seen in The Further Misadventures of Cliff Booth.
extrait: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth takes place eight years after Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood and follows the life of stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) after Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) moves out of the country. Booth now performs dirty odd jobs for celebrities to keep himself afloat, and his life is just as exciting as it was before. Tarantino decided not to direct this movie, as he wants his 10th and (allegedly) final film to be something bigger. He wrote the script and handed it to David Fincher, known for Se7en (1995), Fight Club (1999), and Gone Girl (2014). Polygon's Jake Kleinman noted that this director swap gave the movie a "moody, noir-ish score"; it was still "beautiful to behold, and Fincher's camera luxuriates in that aesthetic even more than Tarantino." What fans noticed was the use of generative AI in the film, but the director has an explanation of sorts. Speaking on The Ringer's "Big Picture" podcast, David Fincher admitted to relying on AI tools in the post-production of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. In previous movies, Fincher, a known perfectionist, would make actors shoot scenes over 50 times. Fincher says AI helps him achieve creative focusand easily address imperfectionswithout having to reshoot a scene. In The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, Fincher only kept actors an additional four to five days to re-record lines over scenes. Afterward, he was able to sync up "the best thing on the eye" with "the best thing on the ear" and create the perfect take. “It’ll still be based on real human beings,” Fincher said. “It’ll still be based on real humans, the way humans move and how they traverse a set and how they, how they pull up their trousers before they sit down or take their coat off. All that stuff will be there, people will only have to do it 15 times.” While Fincher notes that AI is a great way to handle small flaws in a take, such as making sure "that hair doesn’t cross right in front of your cornea," it seems to have been used to make more noticeable changes. This interview took place before allegations emerged about The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth utilizing blatant generative AI, such as a scene with a carriage with a horse on the wrong side. Previously, speaking to the Los Angeles Times, Finch said that he didn’t fear the emergence of AI as a filmmaking tool: “It exists.
